newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Axe falls on 62,000 rats in rural Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Axe falls on 62,000 rats in rural Vietnam.

text.p: A provincial official in northern Vietnam said on Saturday that local villagers near Hanoi had handed in 62,629 rat tails following a cash-for-rodent campaign.
He said 100 dong (less than one cent) had been paid for each rat or mouse tail produced.
"It was quite successful. We burnt the tails in a large pit. No people got hurt but a few chickens and dogs died," he told Reuters.
Communal purges on rats and mice, which eat staple crops such as rice and sweet potatoes, are common in Vietnam.
